title: CostShield: latency fence and locality-aware routing for safe batching/caching rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a unified guardrail layer (CostShield) that enforces latency/throughput SLOs during automated batching and KV-caching configuration recommendations and staged applies. The feature combines local limiters, SLO-aware routing, and streaming anomaly detection so cost-driven config changes (e.g., larger batch windows, more aggressive cache TTLs, quantization profiles) cannot silently regress customer-facing latency SLOs.
background: We've shipped heuristic batching/caching recommendations in the optimizer, but customers and internal dogfood runs show occasional regressions in p95/p99 latency when recommendations are applied at scale or in heterogenous traffic. Existing rollback is manual or coarse-grained. We need a real-time guardrail that: 1) limits the blast radius of aggressive optimizations, 2) routes traffic to safe variants when anomalies occur, and 3) supports automated rollback with evidence for audits.
proposed_solution: CostShield has three cooperating subsystems: (A) Local limiters: per-model and per-tenant token/sessions limiters, inflight-window ceilings and dynamic per-batch size caps that adapt to observed queue backlog; (B) SLO-aware router: routes requests preferentially to configurations/models with historical headroom for the target SLO and implements an automated fallback to baseline models when risk thresholds are crossed; (C) Stream anomaly detector: continuous EWMA + MAD-based detectors on latency percentiles, error rate, and throughput distributions to trigger rapid circuit actions and rollback. The orchestrator will run staged applies (shadow => micro-canary => widen) with automatic verification gates and audit logs for approvals.
design_decisions: Use EWMA (alpha=0.2) on p95/p99 to detect fast-moving regressions rather than relying solely on windowed averages
Combine MAD (median absolute deviation) and z-score thresholds to balance sensitivity and false positives across customers with skewed traffic patterns
Enforce two-tier limiters: static hard caps (safety floor) and adaptive soft caps that back off proportionally to observed p95 increase
Route by policy priority: user-configured pin > SLO headroom score > region latency delta > cost delta
All rollouts must start with a shadow phase (100% traffic shadowed, 0% served) to verify correctness of batching/caching in production environment
Automatic rollback window is 5 minutes after a triggered anomaly for micro-canary and 15 minutes for widened canary; operators can extend with documented justification
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Unit + integration tests in CI for limiter and router logic (blocking)
Stage 1: Internal dogfood cluster run with synthetic heavy-tail traffic patterns for 48h (smoke + soak)
Stage 2: Shadow pass for target customers where optimizer recommendations are generated and compared to baseline metrics for 2 rolling hours
Stage 3: Micro-canary (0.5% traffic) with automatic monitor for 10 minutes; abort if p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.2 OR error_rate +0.5% absolute
Stage 4: Step increases 0.5% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automated verification gates and incremental hold times (15m, 30m, 1h)
Stage 5: Global enable with periodic recompute of limiters and scheduled review after 24h and 7d
monitoring_and_alerts: Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, per-tenant token throughput (tokens/s), queue depth, batching distribution (batch sizes), KV-cache hit rate, model error rate
Alert rule: Immediate SEV2 if p99 exceeds baseline by >1.5x for 3 consecutive 1m buckets
Alert rule: Auto-circuit (rollback to baseline) if error_rate increases by >0.5 percentage points and sustained for 2 consecutive windows
Anomaly scoring: combine weighted z-scores (latency 0.5, errors 0.3, throughput 0.2); trigger protective routing when score > 3.0
Dashboard: per-release 'CostShield' lane that shows applied configs, canary cohorts, rollback history, and cost delta vs baseline (tokens and GPU-hours)
acceptance_criteria: E2E tests validate that when synthetic 3x latency spike is injected, CostShield circuit trips and router shifts 90%+ of traffic to baseline within 30s
Canary auto-abort triggers on metric thresholds defined in rollout_plan without operator intervention in 95% of simulated fault runs
Observed median cost savings for optimizer recommendations on dogfood workloads is >= 8% with no SLO regressions over 24h
All applied config changes are recorded in audit logs with diff, triggering user-visible notification and rollback reason
Monitoring dashboard surfaces per-tenant evidence for any rollback (metric diffs + sample traces)
